Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. ## What this changes This PR replaces Lit rendering for boards, dashboards, plugin views, Portals, and Systems with Solid 2. **Example:** Reorder two loaded dashboard widgets containing an unsent draft. - **Before:** Lit renders the widgets and retains their iframe state. - **After:** Solid renders the widgets while preserving iframe identity and draft state. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Useful migration with inspected visual evidence, one unresolved P2 regression, and incomplete validation of the rewritten authority boundary. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Real behavior proof is necessary before merge. See [Before merge](#before-merge). | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Security review found an item that needs attention. | ## Product **Kind:** Refactor · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Users should retain existing page appearance, widget drafts, iframe identity, and interactions throughout the Solid migration. **Reason:** The maintainer-directed migration replaces the registered Lit implementations and preserves existing domain and SDK owners without new settings or storage. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 5 items remain** Keep this PR open: the maintainer-directed migration remains distinct work, but the prior board translation regression is unresolved. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `337bea708f613301aaa9067c74978f4b4015e6e3` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Authority-chain proof required: supply redacted browser logs or a diagnostic recording showing an active native-plugin request succeeding and retained handles rejected before Gateway I/O after session reassignment, view removal, and registration replacement, including delayed invocation after retirement; screenshots support visual parity, while the inspected retirement tests mock the request boundary. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. - [ ] **Use reactive translations throughout the ported board renderers (P2)** - This prior finding remains unresolved: changing the UI language while a pending widget is mounted leaves “Needs approval,” its action labels, and widget menu text in the previous language. These components import t from i18n/index.ts, which reads plain state without subscribing to locale changes; the replaced Lit parent supplied that subscription through I18nController. Use lib/reactive/i18n.ts in board-widget-capabilities.solid.tsx, board-widget-cell-render.solid.tsx, board-widget-cell.solid.tsx, board-mcp-app-content.tsx, board-document.tsx, and the frame's JSX translation expressions. - [ ] **Resolve security review attention item** - Native-plugin handle retirement needs final-effect validation; no concrete authorization bypass was established. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk** - The rewritten native-plugin lifecycle must preserve revocation of retained operator-authority handles across session reassignment, registration replacement, and view removal. - [ ] **Explain or restore the original intent of Board locale refresh** - unknown: The replaced Lit elements inherit automatic locale refresh from OpenClawLitElement; file history was inspected, but the original subscription's introduction was not established. ## Findings - [P2] Use reactive translations throughout the ported board renderers — `ui/src/components/board/board-widget-capabilities.solid.tsx:3` ### Provenance - `Board locale refresh` changes intended behavior without addressing why it exists (unknown: The replaced Lit elements inherit automatic locale refresh from OpenClawLitElement; file history was inspected, but the original subscription's introduction was not established.) ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Missing a browser/Gateway trace showing allowed native-plugin I/O and rejection of retained handles after reassignment, removal, and registration replacement.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The Control UI consumes Gateway state and plugin registrations, renders browser pages, and routes interactions through existing domain and SDK owners. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Gateway state] --> B[Domain owners] B --> C[Reactive projections] C --> D[Solid bridge and views] D --> E[Browser DOM and frames] E --> F[Scoped plugin host] F --> A ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Complete the existing Solid cutover while restoring reactive board translations and preserving the established plugin retirement boundary. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source establishes the locale regression: mount a pending board widget in English, then change language; nonreactive translation expressions retain English labels despite the locale notification. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The bridge-based cutover follows the existing migration architecture, but the board renderers must consume the shared reactive translation adapter. Full review comments: - [P2] Use reactive translations throughout the ported board renderers — `ui/src/components/board/board-widget-capabilities.solid.tsx:3` This prior finding remains unresolved: changing the UI language while a pending widget is mounted leaves “Needs approval,” its action labels, and widget menu text in the previous language. These components import t from i18n/index.ts, which reads plain state without subscribing to locale changes; the replaced Lit parent supplied that subscription through I18nController. Use lib/reactive/i18n.ts in board-widget-capabilities.solid.tsx, board-widget-cell-render.solid.tsx, board-widget-cell.solid.tsx, board-mcp-app-content.tsx, board-document.tsx, and the frame's JSX translation expressions. Confidence: 0.99 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.91 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant.
